summary: Timothy Lenz is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington under Richard G. Salomon and Collett Cox, later holding posts there, including as a professor (attested 2017) and faculty member (attested 2026).

Timothy Lubin works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University and Harvard University. His posts include lecturer at Harvard (1994–1996) and the University of Virginia (1996–1997), and assistant professor at Washington and Lee University (1997).
Tina Rasmussen is an active figure in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under traditional teacher Pa-Auk Sayadaw and completed an MA under the supervision of Christian K. Wedemeyer.

Tinatin Aleksandrovna Chavchavadze (1928–1997) was a linguist and scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. She studied at Tbilisi State University, taught there (1956–1958), and worked at the Institute of Linguistics and the Institute of Oriental Studies.

Tine Van Overberghe is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She earned her bachelor's degree at Ghent University (2015–2020), became an assistante diplômée at the University of Lausanne in 2022, and was a PhD student there in 2023.

Tine Vekemans is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She completed an MA in Oriental Languages and Cultures at Ghent University (2003–2007), where she was attested in 2026 as the Ācārya Mahāprajña Chair for Jain Studies.

Tirtha Halder is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He earned degrees from the University of Gour Banga, Jadavpur University, Baba Saheb Ambedkar Education University, and Visva-Bharati University, before pursuing a PhD in Sanskrit at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2022.

Tirumalai Krishnamacharya (1888–1989) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Queen's College, Benares, the University of Mysore, and under Ramamohana Brahmachari, later teaching at Maharaja's Sanskrit College, Mysore (1931) and Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College.

Tissa Rajapatirana (1933–2021) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the Australian National University (1966–1974) under Jan Willem de Jong and later held a post in its Department of South Asian and Buddhist Studies.

Tista Biswas is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies under the supervision of Subuddhi Charan Goswami. As of 2026, she holds the post of Sir William Jones Research Fellow in Sanskritic Studies at The Asiatic Society.

Tiziana Pontillo (born 1969) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She completed her PhD at the University of Milan (1996–2000), studied at the University of Cagliari, and became Full Professor of Sanskrit Language and Literature there in 2022.
Todar Mall was an Indologist who pursued his academic studies under the tutelage of Arthur Anthony Macdonell and Hermann Jacobi.
Todd A. Gibson is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Indiana University Bloomington, earning a PhD attested in 1991, and studied under György Kara.

Todd Thornton Lewis works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University under Theodore Riccardi Jr., Ainslie T. Embree, and others, later serving as a professor of humanities and world religions at the College of the Holy Cross.

Tokan Tada (1890–1967) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Sera Monastery (1913–1923), was a lecturer at Tohoku University (1925), and held posts at the University of Tokyo (1924) and Toyo Bunko (1956).

Toke Lindegaard Knudsen works in Indology and the history of science. He completed doctoral studies under David Pingree and Kim Plofker, later holding posts at Brown University, the University of Copenhagen, the Indian National Science Academy, and SUNY Oneonta.

Tokio Takata (born 1949) is a sinologist, linguist, and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University and the EHESS, serving as an associate professor and professor at Kyoto University (1983–2014) and later as a professor at Fudan University.

Tokugen Sakai (1912–1996) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Komazawa University and Kyoto University, and under Kodo Sawaki. He held posts as professor emeritus at Komazawa University (1949–1987) and as a lecturer at Eihei-ji (1977–1987).

Tokuno Oda (1860–1911) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Otani University, and under Gaju Ikehara and Junjirō Takakusu. He taught at Fukui Chugakko and later served as a Dozent at Toyo University.

Tokuryu Yamauchi (1890–1982) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Freiburg under Kitaro Nishida, Edmund Husserl, and Martin Heidegger. He held professorships at Hitotsubashi University, Kyoto University, and Ryukoku University.
